raw_response:
I am old now, so I do not chase fancy things. I farm mostly the way that has kept the family fed and given us some cash over the years. On the wheat-maize land, I will still do wheat and then maize right after harvest, because that is the safest for me here. Cotton I keep on part of the land because if grain price is not good, cotton can still bring some money. I watch what the neighbors do, and around here people still put a bit more fertilizer on wheat than on maize because wheat shows it fast if it is hungry. I also cannot spend too much at once, because some people in the family work outside and cash is not always in my hand when I want it.

For wheat, I will not plant too early, just around early October like usual. I use improved seed that people nearby have been using, not the most expensive one. I put base fertilizer before sowing, then one more topdressing in spring if the wheat looks a little yellow. Water from the well costs money, but wheat in our place usually needs a few turns, so I will irrigate at key times and not waste water. After wheat harvest in June, I will hurry to plant summer maize on the same land. There is no time for heavy tillage, so I keep it simple and fast. Maize I fertilize once at planting and once when it grows up, but a bit less than wheat. Cotton I keep on a smaller area. Cotton takes more hand work, but I know how to manage it. I will not push too much fertilizer there, just enough for a steady crop, and I will spray only when I really see pests.
